m:raekoja: The square can be seen for free at any hour. The Town Hall tower normally opens only in summer (about €4, from a guide: not open in autumn and winter). From 20 November 2026 to 6 January 2027 the square hosts the Christmas market, open every day from 10am to 8pm (source: visittallinn.ee). The Town Council Pharmacy (Raeapteek) costs about €2 (to be confirmed).
m:toompea: The cathedral is free; hours from an official source (visitestonia.com) are only published for summer (1 May–30 September, about 8am–6pm); winter hours need checking. Enter respectfully dressed and in silence. The Kohtuotsa and Patkuli viewpoints are always free. Toompea Castle can only be seen from outside.
m:oleviste: From the official website oleviste.ee: from 1 April to 31 October open every day from 10am to 6pm, last entry to the tower at 5:30pm, with a lunch break during the day. After 31 October the church and platform close for winter, so from 1 November you can't go up (exact period to be confirmed). Ticket €10, reduced €5. Access may be limited during services.
m:kiek: From the museum's website (linnamuuseum.ee): from October to April open Tuesday to Sunday from 11am to 6pm, closed on Mondays; from May to September every day. Entry to the whole museum €16 (reduced €10); the bastion tunnels alone cost €10 (reduced €6); the Maiden's Tower €5. A guided tour in Italian costs €60 per group, plus a ticket each.
m:viru: The towers and the street are free at any hour. The workshops in St Catherine's Passage are normally open Tuesday to Saturday from 10am to 6pm and often closed on Mondays (from a guide: to be confirmed).
m:kadriorg: The park is free to visit at all hours. From October to April the Kadriorg Art Museum is open Tuesday from 10am to 6pm, Wednesday from 10am to 8pm, Thursday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm, and closed on Mondays (from the Estonian museums website muuseumikaart.ee). I couldn't find the ticket price: check kadriorumuuseum.ekm.ee.
m:kumu: Open Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm, Thursday until 8pm, closed on Mondays (from the Estonian museums website and a local listing: to be confirmed on kumu.ekm.ee). Tickets cost from €11 to €16 depending on the current exhibition (the website doesn't say which is which: to be confirmed). On «museum nights» entry costs €1, after 6pm.
m:lennusadam: From the official website (meremuuseum.ee): from October to April open Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm, closed on Mondays; the ticket office closes 30 minutes before. Ticket €14 (reduced €7, family €28; children up to 8 go free). Closed on 24 December 2026 and 1 January 2027; on 25, 26 and 31 December open from 10am to 5pm.
m:telliskivi: Free to walk at any hour; shops and venues have their own hours, usually from 10–11am into the evening. I haven't checked the Saturday flea market (to be confirmed).
m:kalamaja: The market is open Monday to Saturday from 9am to 7pm and Sunday from 9am to 5pm (visitestonia.com). The wooden houses and streets of Kalamaja are free to see.
vd:kompressor: The pancake pub, in the heart of the old town: big thin pannkoogid, sweet or savoury, filled with meat, mushrooms or jam. Generous portions and honest prices for the centre.
vp:kompressor: A filled pancake usually costs €6–9 (menu not seen). Hours from visitestonia.com, to be confirmed.
vd:rataskaevu: A modern Estonian restaurant on a side street, with bread baked on site. Fish, meat and seasonal vegetable dishes in a warm place that locals use too.
vp:rataskaevu: A main course is around €15–24 (estimate from guides, menu not seen). Hours from visitestonia.com, to be confirmed.
vd:hellhunt: A quiet, unpretentious pub with 10 beers on tap and about fifty in bottles: the house beers Maja Hele (pale) and Tume (dark) are the most ordered. Sandwiches and pub dishes.
vp:hellhunt: A pub dish is around €10–16 and a beer €4–6 (estimate, menu not seen). Hours from visitestonia.com, to be confirmed.
vd:maiasmokk: The city's historic café, open since 1864 and almost unchanged for more than a century: handmade pastries, cakes and sweets. Inside there's also the marzipan room, with a small display of marzipan figures.
vp:maiasmokk: A coffee with a slice of cake is around €6–9 (menu not seen). Hours from visitestonia.com, to be confirmed.
vd:rost: A small bakery in the Rotermann quarter, in an old industrial building, with sourdough bread, sandwiches and pastries. Famous for its cinnamon rolls: it's small and often crowded.
vp:rost: A cinnamon roll with a coffee is around €5–8 (estimate, menu not seen). It doesn't appear to open on Sundays: hours from visitestonia.com, to be confirmed.
vd:fhoone: Telliskivi's signature venue, in an old factory: breakfasts, soups, international dishes with lots of vegetarian and vegan options, craft beers and cocktails. A young, relaxed atmosphere.
vp:fhoone: A main course is around €10–16 (estimate from guides, menu not seen). Hours from visitestonia.com, to be confirmed.
vd:baltijaam: The covered market next to the station: on the ground floor a street-food area with about twenty stalls, fresh fish and meat, vegetables and local produce. A good place for a quick lunch among locals.
vp:baltijaam: A street-food meal usually costs €6–12 (estimate from guides, stalls not seen). Hours from visitestonia.com, to be confirmed.
vd:pohjala: The Põhjala craft brewery in the Noblessner quarter, by the sea: 24 beers on tap and a Texas-style barbecue menu, with hot sandwiches, salads and desserts. Their porters and barrel-aged beers are the highlight.
vp:pohjala: A barbecue dish is around €13–20 (estimate, menu not seen). Closed on Mondays: hours from visitestonia.com, to be confirmed.
vd:katharinenthal: A historic café-restaurant next to the swan pond and the garden of Kadriorg Palace: cakes, coffee and pastries, with the cinnamon rolls locals love.
vp:katharinenthal: A coffee with a slice of cake is around €6–9 (estimate, menu not seen). Hours from visitestonia.com; the position on the map is approximate: to be confirmed.
cd:cittamuseo: The city's history in a medieval merchant's house.
cd:raekoda: The Town Hall tower, with the view over the square.
cx:raekoda: Only open in summer: check the calendar.
cd:openair: Estonian wooden farmhouses, mills and churches, in a park by the sea.
cx:openair: It's about 7 km from the centre.
cd:kgb: The hotel's surveillance room where foreign guests were spied on.
cd:teletorn: An observation deck at 170 metres, with a glass floor.
cx:teletorn: It's in Pirita, about 9 km from the centre.
cd:fatmargaret: The history of Baltic ships, inside a 16th-century tower.
cd:fotografiska: Contemporary photography in a former power station in the Telliskivi quarter.
